limitations: Byte-perfect transfer proves the backend file equals the client file; it cannot prove the original recording had no dropped frames.

If frames were dropped and the video was then re-encoded with regenerated constant-rate timestamps, the gap evidence is erased; without an external reference (e.g. capture-side frame counter) such drops are not detectable from timestamps.
Duplicate detection compares 32x18 grayscale thumbnails; very subtle motion can look identical.

reference.conclusion: backend decodes the same number of frames the client had before upload: every anomaly above pre-dates the transfer

transfer.meaning: Every chunk and the whole file matched the client's SHA-256. Any issue reported below therefore existed in the source file and is NOT a transfer error.
